newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds marginally up, await Tietmeyer speech.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds marginally up, await Tietmeyer speech.

text.p: Irish bonds were marginally up in thin late trade on Tuesday as the market awaited a speech by the President of the Bundesbank Tietmeyer at 1700 GMT, dealers said.
This follows comments by a Bundesbank official, Edgar Meister, earlier that a higher dollar might be more appropriate.
The dollar was at 1.4990 marks late on Tuesday, far below the heady levels of 1.54 marks attained in October.
"The Tietmeyer speech could be interesting," one dealer said.

By 1608 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had risen 12 pence from Monday's close to 106.35 to yield 6.03 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 10p to 107.95 to yield 6.73 percent.
"The Irish market is just marginally better with the short-end performing better than in the 10-year area where we have seen a few sellers," one dealer said.

"Against bunds we are performing just below 100 basis points at the moment while we are still looking a bit expensive against the UK..In the five-year area we are about 117/118 basis points below the UK and in the 10-year about 88 below," he said.
Dealers said market focus was likely to be on the U.S. on Wednesday ahead of the release of October producer prices data at 1330 GMT.
The forecast is for a rise of 0.2 percent on September and for a rise of 2.8 percent year-on-year.
